text: Thank you, District 2. The work continues — together.

heading: Thank you, District 2!
text: District 2 re-elected Commissioner Marleine Bastien outright — 78% of the vote, won in one round, no runoff. That mandate belongs to every family, senior, and small business that believed in this work. Now we get back to it.

heading: Results for District 2
text: Since taking office in 2022, Commissioner Bastien has delivered for the families, seniors, and small businesses of Miami-Dade District 2.

heading: Affordable Housing & Anti-Displacement
text: More than 1,800 new homes at every income level, including 155 dedicated senior units and 800+ homes for families earning 30 to 60% of area median income, plus a Community Benefits policy that gives residents a real voice in development.

heading: Parks & Wellness
text: The Health is Wealth Initiative revitalized Oak Grove Park and Sidney Wynn Park at Arcola with nature-based playgrounds, new irrigation, and landscaping.

heading: Small Business & Jobs
text: The Mom & Pop Grant Program funds equipment, inventory, insurance and security for local shops, alongside facade improvements, an innovation hub, and workforce programs through five Community Redevelopment Agencies.

heading: Seniors & Families
text: $1.9 million for the Older Adults Home Modification Program lets residents 62 and older age safely at home, and the Eviction Diversion Program brings legal help to families facing eviction.

heading: Clean, Healthy Neighborhoods
text: The county’s first Solid Waste Cares Program helps customers facing financial hardship with their fees, paired with new recycling and waste-diversion incentives to keep District 2 clean.

heading: Civic & Financial Empowerment
text: The county’s first Civic Engagement Academy teaches residents how their government works, while the Financial Literacy Program helps families build savings and lasting stability.

heading: A lifetime of service
text: Marleine Bastien came to Miami from Pont-Benoit, Haiti, at 22 years old. She built her life here as a licensed clinical social worker and spent decades fighting for working families.

heading: A lifetime of service
text: In 1991 she founded FANM (Family Action Network Movement), which became South Florida’s leading advocate for immigrant women and families. In 2022, she made history as the first Haitian-American woman elected to the Miami-Dade County Commission.

heading: A lifetime of service
text: Today she chairs the County’s Housing Committee and she is just getting started. The work is not done.

heading: Affordable housing & anti-displacement
text: Keep building homes families can actually afford, and protect renters from being pushed out of the neighborhoods they built.

heading: A local economy for small business
text: Grow the Mom & Pop grant program and bring jobs and investment to District 2’s commercial corridors.

heading: Modern infrastructure
text: Fix the aging roads, drainage, and water systems that have been neglected in our community for far too long.

heading: Jobs & opportunity for all
text: Expand job training and real pathways so every family can build lasting financial security.
